problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x)={cos}^{4}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ on the interval $[0,\pi ].$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Average Value of a Function Over a Given Interval
examples.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x) = x - 2$ on the interval $[-2, 4].$
examples.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4-(-2)}{\int }_{-2}^{4}x-2\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-2x){|}_{-2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[(\frac{{4}^{2}}{2}-2(4))-(\frac{(-2)^{2}}{2}-2(-2))] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[(8-8)-(2+4)] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(0-6) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find the value of $c$ that satisfies the mean value theorem for integrals for $f(x)=3{x}^{2}-2$ on the interval $[1,3].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for the integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3-1}{\int }_{1}^{3}(3{x}^{2}-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{2}\cdot ({x}^{3}-2x)|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[({3}^{3}-2\cdot 3)-({1}^{3}-2\cdot 1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(21+1) \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =11 \\ 3{c}^{2}-2 & =11 \\ 3{c}^{2} & =13 \\ {c}^{2} & =\frac{13}{3} \\ c & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{13}{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

However, since $c\in [1,3],$ we take only $c=\sqrt{\frac{13}{3}}.$
